problem: Research on integrating LLMs with 3D data is scattered and nascent (mostly since 2023), with no systematic survey of how LLMs process, understand, reason over and generate 3D data, and no consolidated comparison across 3D-language benchmarks.
motivation: The physical world is 3D, and LLM strengths (in-context learning, reasoning, open-vocabulary ability, world knowledge) could advance spatial understanding for embodied AI. A taxonomy and a meta-analysis are needed to see what has been achieved and what is missing.
key_idea: A survey that proposes a taxonomy of 3D-LLM methods by the role the LLM plays (task analyzer, multi-task learner, multi-modal interface, embodied agent, generator), and meta-analyzes results on common 3D vision-language benchmarks.
insight: The meta-analysis (Tab. benchmarks) shows that generalist 3D-LLMs, especially multi-view/video-based ones such as Ross3D, now beat specialists on ScanQA and SQA3D. They still trail humans substantially: a 40.6% gap on ScanQA EM and 30.1% on SQA3D EM. Bottlenecks named are the loss of spatial information when 3D features are projected to 1D text tokens, scarce 3D-text paired data, and text-only metrics that hide hallucination.
method: Taxonomy: categorises 3D-LLM methods by LLM role (task analyzer, multi-task learner, multi-modal interface, embodied agent for planning/navigation/manipulation, generation assistant), with a comparison table over 3D geometry, vision model, LLM base, fine-tuning, alignment module and hardware.
Task and metric review: five task groups (captioning, grounding, conversation/QA, embodied agents, text-to-3D generation) with their metrics (CIDEr/BLEU, Acc@IoU, EM, SR/SPL, CD/FID).
Background on 3D representations (point cloud, voxel, mesh, NeRF, 3DGS), LLMs and PEFT, and 2D VLMs/VFMs.
Review of 3D tasks with 2D VLMs: open-vocabulary 3D understanding, text-driven 3D generation, end-to-end 3D-language architectures.
Dataset survey: 3D-text datasets by task, real vs synthetic, and annotation type (human, template, model).
Meta-analysis: table comparing specialists and generalists (point-based and multi-view) on ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA and SQA3D, with a model-vs-human gap.
Challenges and opportunities: 3D representations, 3D-centric pre-training, dynamic/4D understanding, RL for spatial reasoning, data scarcity, evaluation, safety.
numbers_note: Survey; no own-method results. The aggregated benchmark table covers ScanRefer, ScanQA, SQA3D and similar (not navigation) and reproduces other papers' numbers, so it is not recorded.
results: The meta-analysis shows generalist 3D-LLMs surpassing specialists. The best model (Ross3D/VeBrain) reaches ScanRefer Acc@0.25 of 66.4, ScanQA CIDEr of 107.0 and SQA3D EM of 63.0. Humans remain far ahead, with gaps of 40.6% on ScanQA EM and 30.1% on SQA3D EM.
limitations: Navigation is covered only briefly, and the datasets/metrics for navigation and manipulation are deferred to other surveys.
The meta-analysis uses numbers copied from original papers under differing protocols and metrics, so comparisons are not controlled.
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
